title: Make pipeline chunk-scope admission atomic with stage claims
description:
## Finding

Pipeline file-scope exclusion is not part of the atomic claim transaction. `session open --stage --chunk` first reads active rows and chunk files through `chunk_gate()`, releases that read, then separately executes `claim_dispatch()` under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Two concurrent Leads/workers can therefore both observe no overlapping sibling and both insert overlapping chunks. The nominally safe `thegn dispatch claim --chunk` path is worse: it records `chunk_path` but never calls `chunk_gate()` at all.

The stage concurrency limit remains atomic, but that does not protect file ownership when the configured stage allows two or more workers - the exact case chunk scopes are meant to make safe.

## Evidence

* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/session.rs:952-958`: `chunk_gate()` runs before the claim and outside its transaction.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/session.rs:975-995`: `claim_dispatch()` is a later, separate operation.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/dispatch.rs:550-584`: the `dispatch claim` implementation passes `chunk_path` to `claim_dispatch()` without any scope validation.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/cmd/dispatch.rs:407-518`: `chunk_gate()` performs a non-transactional `list_dispatches()` plus filesystem reads.
* `crates/thegn-core/src/db_dispatch.rs:267-350`: `claim_dispatch()` atomically enforces duplicate/stage capacity only; it has no normalized chunk scope or overlap/`after` decision.

Interleaving: A and B carry overlapping `files:` at a stage with concurrency 2; both complete `chunk_gate()` against the same empty roster; A claims and commits; B then claims and commits because capacity remains. Both edit the same files despite the advertised refusal.

## Constraints

* File-scope/`after:` validation, stage capacity, duplicate handling, and row insertion must have one authoritative admission boundary.
* Do not hold a SQLite write transaction across arbitrary attacker-controlled or slow filesystem I/O if normalized scope can be validated and materialized first.
* A chunk file changing between validation and claim must not let the stored claim misrepresent what was authorized; bind the claim to content/hash or store the normalized scope.
* Forced overlap remains explicit and auditable, never the default `session open` behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every public row-creation path carrying a chunk (`session open`, `dispatch claim`, and retained `dispatch put`) uses the same scope admission implementation.
2. Scope overlap, `after:` satisfaction, stage capacity, duplicate decision, and insert are serialized as one logical transaction.
3. A claim is bound to the exact normalized scope/content reviewed; post-check file replacement cannot alter its effective ownership.
4. Two concurrent overlapping claims at concurrency >=2 yield exactly one accepted row and one explicit retryable refusal.
5. Disjoint chunks can still claim concurrently up to the stage budget.
6. Forced overlap records actor/reason and is visible in roster/JSON audit output.

## Verification

* Add a barrier-controlled two-connection race test for overlapping chunks and a disjoint control case.
* Test `dispatch claim --chunk` directly; it must no longer bypass scope validation.
* Test a chunk-file replacement between parse and claim.
* Run dispatch/session/pipeline smoke tests and `just quick`.

## Dependency mapping

This is an independent data-consistency fix. It can land before the authority work (THE-208).
